seedTerms: A difficult decision with no easy way

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Bedside Manner
jokes.joke: My surgeon was incredibly empathetic. Right before the operation he held my hand and said, “I know you’re scared. I am too.” I said, “No, no—this is one of those jobs where I need you to lie to me. I don’t want emotional honesty from the guy holding the scalpel. I want, ‘Routine procedure.’ I want you bored enough to be thinking about lunch.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Trail Marker
jokes.joke: My brother's a surgeon, so he hikes like he operates. We hit a fork in the trail and he goes, 'Don't touch anything, I need to scrub in.' Then he stood there for twenty minutes, washed his hands in a creek, and said, 'The map is fine. The patient is the real problem.' The patient was me. I had a blister.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Bedside Manner
jokes.joke: People say they want a doctor with a warm bedside manner. Not me. I want my surgeon to be the most fussy, insufferable person on earth. I don't want a 'chill' guy anywhere near my open chest cavity. I want a man who sends his soup back because the parsley is asymmetrical. If you're holding my actual beating heart, I don't need a friend. I need a guy who irons his own shoelaces and ruins family vacations.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Trail Standards
jokes.joke: I'm the fussiest guy on any hiking trail. Three pairs of socks, gaiters, a backup rain shell, the whole catalog. Halfway up I stop to adjust my pack straps for the fourth time and announce the humidity feels aggressive. My friends finally pointed at a fork in the path. Left was the scenic overlook. Right was the one where they leave me. I took the right.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Second Opinion
seedTermsUsed: A difficult decision with no easy way
jokes.joke: I needed surgery, and the surgeon said, 'This is a tough call. There’s really no easy way to do this.' That’s not what you want to hear from a guy already holding a marker near your chest. I said, 'What are my options?' He said, 'The medical one... or I can just write 'Good luck' and let fate finish the procedure.'

scores.comment: Clear premise and clean seed use, but the surgical hiking analogy is stretched and the blister reveal lands mildly.
Strong, relatable premise with effective escalation; the parsley, shoelaces, and family-vacation details build to a solid finish.
Good self-deprecating turn and concise structure; the fork-in-the-trail payoff is amusing but not especially surprising.
Readable and well framed, but the fate option feels like generic absurdity rather than a sharply earned punchline.
Relatable reversal: the patient wants a bored surgeon, not an honest one. The lunch line lands, but the 'I want lies from my doctor' angle is familiar.
Clear premise, good escalation from the asymmetrical parsley to the ironed shoelaces. 'Ruins family vacations' is a sharp, specific final turn.
The fussy-hiker setup is solid, and 'the one where they leave me' is a decent self-aware turn. The overlook/abandonment fork is a bit predictable and the tag is a little flat.
The marker-near-the-chest image is good, but the ending is muddled. 'Write Good luck and let fate finish' doesn't clearly pay off the setup, and the seed concept is used only as a phrase.
Clean execution of a classic comedic premise. The rhythm is excellent and the final line hits hard, even if the 'scared doctor' angle is a familiar trope.
An amusing mashup of the two concepts. The absurdity of scrubbing in at a creek works well, and the blister reveal provides a solid, grounded punchline.
Very natural stage voice and strong setup details ('humidity feels aggressive'), but the final punchline is a bit of a soft landing.
A competent but slightly cartoonish bit. The long seed phrase feels somewhat wedged into the dialogue rather than organically inspiring the scenario.
Solid premise and clean delivery; lunch-boredom closer earns a real smile.
Fun surgeon-hike analogy undercut by a soft blister payoff.
Specific fussy images escalate cleanly to a strong final line.
Clear setup with a wry fatalistic turn; competent but not memorable.
Strong premise, clear escalation, and a relatable turn on empathy becoming undesirable.
Coherent but feels stitched together; the blister reveal is mild and predictable.
Good comic logic with vivid examples and escalating specifics that support the final image.
Clear character premise and a solid final turn; concise and easy to visualize.
